subject: Bug in annotate() with histograms: renames y axis label from "count"  to "y"

messages.author: eca99c51870663ea
messages.subject: Bug in annotate() with histograms: renames y axis label from "count"  to "y"
parts:
The annotate function is very useful - and thanks Hadley for adding
it. However, I've found that using annotate() changes the y axis label
in a histogram from "count" to "y".

# Generate some numbers
df <- data.frame(first=rnorm(100), second=rnorm(100))

# Histogram: y axis labeled "count"
qplot(first, data=df)
# This changes the axis label from "count" to "y"
qplot(first, data=df) + annotate("text",x=1,y=1,label="my annotation")

# No effect on scatterplot
qplot(first, second, data=df) + annotate("text",x=1,y=1,label="my
annotation")


Also, in histogram, is it possible to rename the y axis from "count"
to something else, or make it go away entirely? Setting ylab doesn't
do anything, which I guess makes sense since the y axis is generated
by counting up the data.

If this forum isn't the right place to report bugs, please let me know
where they should go. I've been running into little ones here and
there as I've gotten familiar with ggplot2.

-Winston

> Also, in histogram, is it possible to rename the y axis from "count"
> to something else, or make it go away entirely? Setting ylab doesn't
> do anything, which I guess makes sense since the y axis is generated

+ ylab(NULL)

removes the y axis label (and the space used by it) entirely.

--Nicholas

messages.subject: Re: Bug in annotate() with histograms: renames y axis label from  "count" to "y"
parts:
I see the issue here... I put the ylab in the qplot arguments instead of alone. I don't know if this is the expected behavior or not.

# Label works
qplot(first, data=df) + annotate("text",x=1,y=1,label="my annotation") + ylab("foo")

# Label doesn't work
qplot(first, data=df, ylab="foo") + annotate("text",x=1,y=1,label="my annotation")

This doesn't touch on the issue of annotate() renaming the y axis from "count" to "y", of course.

-Winston

On Fri, Apr 24, 2009 at 10:17 PM, Nicholas Riley <nri...@gmail.com> wrote:

On Apr 22, 9:49 pm, winston <wins...@stdout.org> wrote:
> Also, in histogram, is it possible to rename the y axis from "count"
> to something else, or make it go away entirely? Setting ylab doesn't
> do anything, which I guess makes sense since the y axis is generated
> by counting up the data.

Works for me.

qplot(first, data=df) + annotate("text",x=1,y=1,label="my annotation")
+ ylab(NULL)

removes the y axis label (and the space used by it) entirely.

--Nicholas
